title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel
talk_summary: Vercel's Andrew Qu describes iterating a data-science agent from a mega-prompt to a chained multi-agent pipeline to a single file-system agent with bash/read/write tools in a sandbox, which roughly doubled eval scores. He then distills recurring query patterns into ~100 reusable 'skills' and packages the whole pattern as a file-convention agent framework (Eve).

takeaways.technique: File-system agent with minimal generic tools instead of prescriptive tool chains
takeaways.what_they_do: Replace bespoke per-stage agents with one agent given a sandbox containing the data/context and only list/read/write/bash tools, letting it explore and self-correct on errors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the big unlock was that it was just a file system ... it had a very minimal set of tools, list file, read file, run bash
takeaways.numbers: eval score 'basically doubled' after switching to file-system agent

takeaways.technique: Collapse chained sub-agents into one stateful agent when handoffs lose context
takeaways.what_they_do: Moved from query→planning→SQL→reporting agents (each getting only a summary) to a single agent managing its own state and looping back on errors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the only thing that the next agent gets is a summary and a small snippet of the previous thing

takeaways.technique: Distill recurring runs into a skills folder via a recurring job
takeaways.what_they_do: A recurring job takes the most recent queries and distills repeated shapes into reusable skills (~100), so each new run starts with prior contextual knowledge instead of from nothing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually have a recurring job that takes the most recent queries and tries to distill them into a skill

takeaways.technique: Small trusted-user rollout to surface real questions evals miss
takeaways.what_they_do: Shipped to a few trusted users early; their real questions exposed gaps the 30%-passing evals didn't cover, motivating the architecture change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we thought this was, you know, nailing 30% of our evals, but we couldn't have anticipated some of the questions
takeaways.numbers: ~30% eval pass rate before the file-system rewrite

takeaways.technique: Run agents in isolated sandboxes with attached files
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent runs in a sandbox pre-loaded with the semantic layer/files; bash tool attached to sandbox for read/write/execute.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it was now going to run in a sandbox. That sandbox would dump the whole semantic layer into it

takeaways.what_they_do: Standardize agent definition as a directory convention (system instructions, skills, tools, channels) so new agents start from the latest best practice instead of from scratch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You should only have to create a skills folder, a tools folder, a channels folder
